problem_statement: The paper frames portfolio optimization as an important finance problem and focuses on understanding how COVID-19 affected the selection of optimal portfolios across different industries. It says the work studies portfolio optimization over pre-COVID and COVID time intervals and compares the results with the classical Markowitz approach.
problem_statement_quotes: Portfolio optimization is one of the important problem classes in finance sector.
it is imperative to understand what kind of impact COVID-19 had on portfolio optimization and how quantum computers can be used in doing so.

In the present work, we employ these algorithms to carry out portfolio optimization for different time intervals (which includes pre and during COVID-19 periods) and unravel the impact of COVID-19 on the same, across different industries.
classical_baseline: The paper treats the classical baseline as Markowitz's modern portfolio theory, and also refers more generally to classical algorithms for identifying optimal portfolios. It explicitly says it compares the quantum results against the classical Markowitz approach.
classical_baseline_quotes: There are several algorithms that have been developed to identify optimum portfolios such as Markowitz model, genetic, firefly, fuzzy approach algorithms and many more.

we have two major objectives namely, i) unravelling the effect of COVID-19 on various portfolios by means of quantum algorithms and compare it with the classical Markowitz's approach and ii) evaluate the quantum algorithms such as VQE and QAOA with reference to the classical Markowitz's theory.
To corroborate the results obtain using quantum algorithms, calculation based on Markowitz’s modern portfolio theory (MPT) has been applied on the datasets using the Qiskit and Python.
classical_difficulty: The paper says the classical algorithms are efficient on classical computers, but are not directly implementable on quantum computers. It also frames portfolio optimization as part of the class of problems that quantum computing may help with because such problems are described as intractable to classical computing.
classical_difficulty_quotes: These algorithms can be in a sense termed classical, implying they can be run efficiently on classical computers.
However, with the advent of quantum computing we are posed with the challenges of implementing these well-known algorithms on these quantum computers.

When quantum computers have about 300 qubits it can process more information than there are total number of atoms in the entire universe. When this happens the stage will be all set to solve problems that are intractable to classical computing one after the other.
business_stakes: The paper says the COVID-19 pandemic had a huge blow on the global economy and left the financial sector almost toppled, and that understanding portfolio behavior during the pandemic helps prepare for future events. It does not quantify business stakes beyond that.
business_stakes_quotes: The unforeseen COVID-19 pandemic delivered a huge blow to the global economy. Especially, it left the financial sector almost toppled.
Understanding the trend in portfolio during the pandemic not only helps in learning how it really evolved, it also helps us prepare for any such possible event in the future.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is a poster-style applied study with clear comparison to Markowitz.
